points.text: Un **TAD** es un conjunto de valores y operaciones definidos **con independencia de la implementación**. En Java, la **interfaz** declara las operaciones y la **clase** que la implementa da el código de cada una (no al revés).

refs.title: NIST DADS · abstract data type
refs.quote: A set of data values and associated operations that are precisely specified independent of any particular implementation.

refs.title: Oracle · Java Tutorials: Defining an Interface
refs.quote: When an instantiable class implements an interface, it provides a method body for each of the methods declared in the interface.

points.text: **Cola** (FIFO): solo se accede al elemento más antiguo; se inserta por el **final (cola)** y se saca por la **cabecera**. Se puede implementar con estructuras dinámicas (listas enlazadas) o con arrays.

refs.title: NIST DADS · queue
refs.quote: A collection of items in which only the earliest added item may be accessed. Basic operations are add (to the tail ) or enqueue and delete (from the head ) or dequeue.

refs.title: NIST DADS · queue
refs.quote: Also known as "first-in, first-out" or FIFO.

refs.title: Oracle Java SE 21 · Queue
refs.quote: In a FIFO queue, all new elements are inserted at the tail of the queue.

refs.title: Oracle Java SE 21 · LinkedList
refs.quote: Doubly-linked list implementation of the List and Deque interfaces.

refs.title: Oracle Java SE 21 · Queue
refs.quote: All Known Implementing Classes: AbstractQueue , ArrayBlockingQueue , ArrayDeque

points.text: **Pila** (LIFO): se puede implementar sobre un **array** (en Java, `ArrayDeque`, más rápida que `Stack`).

refs.title: Oracle Java SE 21 · ArrayDeque
refs.quote: Resizable-array implementation of the Deque interface.

refs.title: Oracle Java SE 21 · ArrayDeque
refs.quote: This class is likely to be faster than Stack when used as a stack

points.text: **Lista enlazada simple**: cada elemento apunta al siguiente. En la **circular**, el último está enlazado con el primero.

refs.title: NIST DADS · linked list
refs.quote: A list implemented by each item having a link to the next item.

refs.title: NIST DADS · circular list
refs.quote: A variant of a linked list in which the nominal tail is linked to the head .

points.text: **Árbol 2-3-4**: árbol B de orden 4; sus nodos internos tienen **2, 3 o 4 hijos**.

refs.title: NIST DADS · 2-3-4 tree
refs.quote: A B-tree of order 4, that is, internal nodes have two, three, or four children

points.text: Recorrido en **preorden**: raíz, subárbol izquierdo, subárbol derecho.

refs.title: NIST DADS · preorder traversal
refs.quote: print(tree.root); preorder(tree.left_subtree); preorder(tree.right_subtree);

points.text: Árboles: el **grado de un nodo** es su número de hijos. Una **hoja** es un nodo sin hijos (nodo externo o terminal). La **profundidad** de un nodo es su distancia a la raíz (la raíz tiene 0) y la **altura** del árbol es la distancia máxima de un nodo a la raíz (un árbol de un solo nodo tiene altura 0).

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · degree
refs.quote: (3) Of a tree node

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · degree
refs.quote: the number of child nodes it has.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · leaf
refs.quote: A node in a tree without any children

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · leaf
refs.quote: Also known as external node, terminal node.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · depth
refs.quote: the distance from the node to the root of the tree

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · depth
refs.quote: The depth of the root is 0. The depth of a node is one plus the depth of its parent

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · height
refs.quote: If a tree has only one node (the root), the height is zero.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · height
refs.quote: the height is the maximum depth of any node.

points.text: Árboles binarios:

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · full binary tree
refs.quote: A binary tree in which each node has exactly zero or two children

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · full binary tree
refs.quote: In other words, every node is either a leaf or has two children.

items.text: **Completo** (*complete*): todos los niveles llenos salvo quizá el último, cuyos nodos están **lo más a la izquierda** posible.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · complete binary tree
refs.quote: A binary tree in which every level (depth), except possibly the deepest, is completely filled.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · complete binary tree
refs.quote: At depth n, the height of the tree, all nodes must be as far left as possible.

items.text: **Perfecto**: todas las hojas a la misma profundidad y todos los nodos internos con grado 2; tiene **2^(h+1) − 1** nodos (h = altura).

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · perfect binary tree
refs.quote: A binary tree with all leaf nodes at the same depth

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · perfect binary tree
refs.quote: All internal nodes have degree 2.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · perfect binary tree
refs.quote: nodes, where n is the height

points.text: Recorridos: **inorden** (simétrico): subárbol izquierdo, raíz, subárbol derecho. **Postorden**: subárboles y al final la raíz. **Por niveles**: la raíz, luego sus hijos, etc. (equivale a una búsqueda en anchura).

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · in-order traversal
refs.quote: Process all nodes of a tree by recursively processing the left subtree, then processing the root

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · in-order traversal
refs.quote: Also known as symmetric traversal.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · postorder traversal
refs.quote: Process all nodes of a tree by recursively processing all subtrees, then finally processing the root

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · level-order traversal
refs.quote: Equivalent to a breadth-first search from the root.

points.text: **Búsqueda en anchura** (BFS): visita los vecinos antes de profundizar; se implementa con una **cola**. **En profundidad** (DFS): baja por los hijos antes que por los hermanos; se implementa fácilmente con **recursión**; en un árbol puede ser **preorden, inorden o postorden**.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · breadth-first search
refs.quote: Any search algorithm that considers neighbors of a vertex

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · breadth-first search
refs.quote: This is typically implemented with a queue

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · depth-first search
refs.quote: Any search algorithm that considers outgoing edges

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · depth-first search
refs.quote: This is easily implemented with recursion

points.text: **Bicola** (*deque*, *double-ended queue*): se inserta y se saca por **ambos extremos**.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · deque
refs.quote: A data structure in which items may be added to or deleted from the head or the tail

refs.title: Java SE 21 API · Deque
refs.quote: A linear collection that supports element insertion and removal at both ends.

points.text: **Diccionario** o **mapa**: guarda valores a los que se accede por una **clave**; en Java, `Map` no admite claves duplicadas y `HashMap` no garantiza el orden.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · dictionary
refs.quote: An abstract data type storing items, or values. A value is accessed by an associated key

refs.title: Java SE 21 API · Map
refs.quote: An object that maps keys to values. A map cannot contain duplicate keys; each key can map to at most one value.

refs.title: Java SE 21 API · Map
refs.quote: others, like the HashMap class, do not.

points.text: **Dijkstra**: caminos más cortos desde un vértice origen a todos los demás en un grafo dirigido **ponderado** (pesos no negativos).

refs.title: NIST DADS · Dijkstra's algorithm
refs.quote: An algorithm to find the shortest paths from a single source vertex to all other vertices in a weighted, directed graph . All weights must be nonnegative.

points.text: **Burbuja**: compara pares **adyacentes** y los intercambia si están desordenados, repitiendo hasta que no haya intercambios; O(n²) en general.

refs.title: NIST DADS · bubble sort
refs.quote: Sort by comparing each adjacent pair of items in a list in turn, swapping the items if necessary, and repeating the pass through the list until no swaps are done.

refs.title: NIST DADS · bubble sort
refs.quote: Complexity is O(n 2 ) for arbitrary data

points.text: **Radix**: ordenación por distribución que reparte los elementos en cubetas según **cada parte de la clave**, una pasada por dígito. Razonamiento: con d pasadas sobre n elementos y k cubetas, el coste es del orden de d·(n+k); con d y k fijos, **lineal** en n. **Heapsort**, en cambio, es O(n log n).

refs.title: NIST DADS · radix sort
refs.quote: A multiple pass distribution sort algorithm that distributes each item to a bucket according to part of the item's key beginning with the least significant part of the key.

refs.title: NIST DADS · heapsort
refs.quote: A sort algorithm that builds a heap , then repeatedly extracts the maximum item. Run time is O(n log n) .

points.text: **Algoritmo voraz**: toma siempre la **mejor solución inmediata (local)**.

refs.title: NIST DADS · greedy algorithm
refs.quote: An algorithm that always takes the best immediate, or local, solution while finding an answer.

points.text: **Quicksort**: elige un **pivote**, parte el resto entre mayores y menores que él y ordena las partes recursivamente. Peor caso **Θ(n²)**, normalmente **O(n log n)**.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · quicksort
refs.quote: Pick an element from the array (the pivot), partition the remaining elements into those greater than and less than this pivot, and recursively sort the partitions.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · quicksort
refs.quote: Quicksort has running time Θ(n²) in the worst case

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · quicksort
refs.quote: but it is typically O(n log n)

points.text: **Kruskal**: calcula el **árbol de expansión mínimo** de un grafo ponderado añadiendo cada vez la arista **más corta** que une dos árboles parciales distintos.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · Kruskal's algorithm
refs.quote: It maintains a set of partial minimum spanning trees, and repeatedly adds the shortest edge in the graph whose vertices are in different partial minimum spanning trees.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · minimum spanning tree
refs.quote: A minimum-weight tree in a weighted graph which contains all of the graph's vertices

points.text: El **método de acceso** define cómo se organizan los datos de un fichero y cómo se guardan y recuperan. Tipos clásicos (ejemplo: VSAM de IBM):

refs.title: IBM z/OS Basic Skills · DFSMSdfp access methods
refs.quote: An access method defines the organization of the data in a data set and the technique by which the data is stored and retrieved.

refs.title: IBM Enterprise PL/I · VSAM organization
refs.quote: Key-sequenced data sets (KSDS) Indexed data set Entry-sequenced data sets (ESDS) Consecutive data set Relative record data sets (RRDS) Regional data set

items.text: **Secuencial**: los registros están en el orden en que se grabaron y se leen en ese orden (ESDS).

refs.title: IBM CICS TS 5.5 · VSAM data sets: KSDS, ESDS, RRDS
refs.quote: Records are held in an ESDS in the order in which they were first loaded into the data set.

refs.title: IBM z/OS XL C/C++ Programming Guide · VSAM types
refs.quote: Entry-Sequenced Data Set (ESDS) is used for data that is primarily accessed in the order it was created (or the reverse order).

items.text: **Indexada**: se accede por una **clave** del registro (KSDS).

refs.title: IBM z/OS XL C/C++ Programming Guide · VSAM types
refs.quote: Key-Sequenced Data Set (KSDS) is used when a record is accessed through a key field within the record

items.text: **Relativa** o **directa**: se accede por el **número de registro** (RRDS).

refs.title: IBM z/OS XL C/C++ Programming Guide · VSAM types
refs.quote: It supports direct access by Relative Record Number (RRN), and sequential access.

points.text: **Dispersión** (*hashing*): una **función hash** convierte la clave en una posición. Hay **colisión** cuando dos claves van a la misma posición; se resuelve con **direccionamiento abierto** (se prueban otras posiciones de la tabla hasta encontrar una libre), **encadenamiento** (listas enlazadas) o un **área de desbordamiento**.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · hash function
refs.quote: A function that maps keys to integers, usually to get an even distribution on a smaller set of values.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · hash table
refs.quote: Having the keys of more than one item map to the same position is called a collision

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · hash table
refs.quote: keeping one special overflow area.

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · open addressing
refs.quote: other positions are computed, giving a probe sequence

refs.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures · chaining
refs.quote: A class of collision resolution schemes in which linked lists handle collisions in a hash table

points.text: **JSON** (RFC 8259): un valor es objeto, array, número o cadena, o uno de los literales **false, null y true** (en minúsculas). En los objetos, cada miembro es **nombre (cadena entre comillas dobles)** `:` valor.

refs.title: RFC 8259 · JSON
refs.quote: A JSON value MUST be an object, array, number, or string, or one of the following three literal names: false null true The literal names MUST be lowercase.

refs.title: RFC 8259 · JSON
refs.quote: member = string name-separator value

refs.title: RFC 4180 · CSV
refs.quote: Each record is located on a separate line, delimited by a line break (CRLF).

refs.title: RFC 4180 · CSV
refs.quote: Fields containing line breaks (CRLF), double quotes, and commas should be enclosed in double-quotes.
